{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of vendor-form Master Services Agreement — verified findings

## Executive summary

We have completed the playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. Eighteen rules were assessed: seven clauses sit at or above our preferred position and need no change, one requires internal review only, and ten items require redlines — including three critical issues.

The critical problems are structural. First, the Agreement contains **no indemnification provision at all**: the numbering jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), leaving Section 20 absent even though Sections 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 all cross-refer to indemnity rights. Second, Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for us, with only a revocable, term-limited licence back — failing both our preferred position and our fallback. Third, the Agreement gives us **no termination-for-convenience right** across a three-year term that also carries a USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" (Section 2.1).

A cluster of one-way restrictions binds us with no counterpart on Vendor: a right-of-first-refusal and matching obligation before we may engage another provider (Section 7.2), a 24-month post-term non-compete covering any competing product in any territory, and a 24-month no-hire covering every Vendor employee (both in Section 12.4). Each of these directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that we have made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment — so the drafting is internally inconsistent as well as off-playbook. Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts, contradicting the New York venue named in Section 28.2. Post-termination transition assistance and data return are also absent, with Section 16.5 deferring Customer Data to a "Section 11" that does not exist in the document.

On the positive side, the limitation of liability (Section 21), assignment and change of control (Section 24), licence grant (Section 13), audit rights (Section 22), auto-renewal mechanics (Section 8.2–8.3), Vendor insurance (Section 18) and the absence of any liquidated damages or termination penalty all meet our preferred position and should be protected in negotiation.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | Section 20 absent (cross-refs at §§ 9.3, 19.4, 19.5, 21.3, 30.5) | No indemnity or hold-harmless anywhere; Section 20 (incl. the § 20.5 IP remedies) is missing while other clauses presuppose it. We insert a new Section 20 at the preferred position. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable; we hold only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence. Fails preferred and fallback; § 13.2 perpetual licence covers only embedded Vendor Technology. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1–21.4 | Mutual cap at greater of 12-month Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; mutual consequential exclusion with direct-damage carve-ins; Excluded Claims outside cap. No redline. |
| 4 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § 9 (Termination) | Only for-cause exits over a three-year term, with § 2.1 take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights". We insert a new § 9.4 (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund). |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Right of first refusal gating our sourcing: no service-category limit, no 12-month sunset, no performance-failure exit. Contradicts § 12.3. |
| 6 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | 24-month post-term non-compete, any competing product or service, any territory, no internal-development or acquisition carve-out. Contradicts § 12.3. |
| 7 | High | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | One-way 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees, expressly overriding general-advertising and unsolicited-application carve-outs. Contradicts § 12.3. |
| 8 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1–24.4 | Affiliate/M&A assignment by us on notice only; Vendor assignment gated; no repricing or termination on our change of control. Favourable — no redline. |
| 9 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1–13.3 | Worldwide grant to us, Affiliates and contractors; perpetual paid-up rights; revocation only for material uncured breach after notice; transferable with a § 24-permitted assignment. |
| 10 | High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 2.1 (and § 27.3, § 7.1) | No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination charge; § 27.3 confirms termination without penalty. Volume exposure handled under MINCOMMIT. |
| 11 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Three-year USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay expressly without reduction or termination rights. Contradicts § 12.3 and § 7.1. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Matching obligation runs against us, unbounded as to product line and time, with no reasonable-comparison carve-outs. Contradicts § 12.3. |
| 13 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 (cf. § 28.2) | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts, outside our accepted forums and inconsistent with the New York County courts named in § 28.2. |
| 14 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 10.1 (and § 16.5) | No transition-assistance obligation and no Customer Data return, export or deletion-certification duty; § 16.5 defers to a Section 11 that does not exist. |
| 15 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1–22.3 | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable, independent auditor under confidentiality; Vendor bears costs below a 5% underpayment; no system access. |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2–8.3 | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension if missed; uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Needs review (internal) | § 19.1–19.5 | Assessed as compliant at the preferred position; the automated duration check is a false negative because "ninety days" is spelled out in § 19.2. Retained as internal evidence; verification did not pass, so no counterparty comment is raised. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1–18.2 | CGL USD 1M/2M, workers' compensation, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, term plus one year, at Vendor's expense; insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities. |

## Walk-away items

The following findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and cannot be signed in their current form:

1. **No Vendor indemnity (Section 20 absent).** The complete absence of an IP and legal-compliance indemnity is walk-away. A new Section 20 is required, including the § 20.5 IP remedies already cross-referenced in § 9.3. No super-cap is needed because § 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims.
2. **No termination for convenience (Section 9), combined with the Section 2.1 take-or-pay.** No convenience exit in a three-year term with a commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights".
3. **Three-year take-or-pay minimum (Section 2.1).** Multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right is the walk-away position; fallback is a single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice and trued up rather than penalised.
4. **Right of first refusal / de facto exclusivity (Section 7.2).** Unlimited scope, no sunset, no performance-based exit across the full three-year term.
5. **Most-favoured-nation matching obligation running against us (Section 7.2).** Wrong direction and unbounded.
6. **24-month post-term non-compete (Section 12.4).** Period exceeds 12 months and scope is unlimited as to product and territory.
7. **24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees (Section 12.4).** True no-hire, all employees, with carve-outs expressly overridden.
8. **Singapore governing law and exclusive Singapore courts (Section 28.1).** Foreign forum outside our accepted list, and internally inconsistent with § 28.2.
9. **No Customer Data return obligation (Sections 10 and 16.5).** The absence of any return, export or deletion duty exposes us to the walk-away scenario of no data return on exit.

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline and comments** covering the ten action items: new Section 20 (Vendor indemnity, claim procedure, § 20.5 IP remedies, narrow Customer indemnity); reversal of Deliverable ownership in § 14.2 with Vendor assignment, preserving Vendor Technology under §§ 14.3 and 13.2; new § 9.4 convenience termination (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund, expressly overriding § 2.1, and confirming Vendor has no convenience right during a term); deletion of the exclusivity/ROFR and MFN matching obligations in § 7.2; deletion of the § 12.4 non-compete; narrowing of the § 12.4 no-hire to a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs; removal of the § 2.1 minimum with fees payable for usage or ordered Services only; conforming § 28.1 to New York law with venue deferred to § 28.2; and a new § 10.3 (six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, Customer Data return in machine-readable form within 30 days, certified deletion).
2. **Flag the drafting inconsistencies to Vendor** alongside the substantive points: the missing Section 20 leaves dangling cross-references in §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5; §§ 2.1, 7.2 and 12.4 each contradict Vendor's own acknowledgements in § 12.3; § 28.1 contradicts § 28.2; and § 16.5 refers to a Section 11 that does not exist. Framing these as internal inconsistencies should make several deletions easier to land.
3. **Confirm the commercial position on volume** with the business owner. If a commitment is genuinely required, we can offer the fallback structure (single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, trued up rather than penalised) rather than the three-year take-or-pay.
4. **Close out the warranty finding internally.** Section 19 is assessed as compliant at the preferred position; the failed check is a false negative on the spelled-out "ninety days" in § 19.2. We will retain the analysis as internal evidence and raise no comment with Vendor. The narrower § 19.3 malicious-code warranty (code "intentionally introduced by Vendor") is noted only, mitigated by the § 17 security obligations, and we would accept it rather than reopen Section 19.
5. **Protect the favourable terms.** Sections 21 (liability), 24 (assignment), 13 (licence), 22 (audit), 8.2–8.3 (renewal) and 18 (insurance) meet or exceed our preferred position; we should resist any repapering of these in exchange for concessions elsewhere.
6. **Escalate if the walk-away items are not resolved.** If Vendor declines to add an indemnity, a convenience exit or a data-return obligation, or insists on the § 7.2 and § 12.4 restrictions, we recommend escalating to the deal sponsor before further drafting rounds."}
